and Operations Committee to order. My name is Dina Griffiths, and I am joined by Ms. Amy Ricardi and Mr. John Pepper, who are my colleagues on the school board. move to approve the minutes of the,

Oh, no consent agenda for this meeting today. Okay, so we move on. Okay. We will now move to our action items, starting with 4.01, Support Services Award of IFB 26-545 Waterford Elementary School Renovation and Addition. May I have a motion to approve item 4.01? I move that the Finance and Operations Committee place this item on the

December 1, 2026 school board consent agenda and recommend to the Loudoun County School Board to approve the contract award of IFB number 26-545, Waterford Elementary School Renovation and Addition to Keller Brothers Inc. in the amount of $27,322,650, and authorizes the chair of the school board to sign the final contract documents upon presentation. Second. Thank you very much. There was a motion by Mr.

Pepper and seconded by Ms. Ricardi. It has been moved and seconded. This item is being presented by Joseph Pascarelli, Director of Construction. Thank you. Thank you, Madam Chair. So we're happy to be able to present this item to you tonight that would allow us to move to construction for the Waterford project. We received bids for the construction of this project on October 15th. We had a competitive bid process with four bidders submitting bids. After reviewing the bids, we worked in partnership with the low

bidder to review their scope in detail, resulting in some cost savings. And with that, we recommend approval to Keller Brothers for this contract. Thank you very much, Mr. Pascarelli. Is there any discussion? Yes, Ms. Ricardi. Thank you, Madam Chair. I just had a quick question because there's a term in here I'm not familiar with, which is value engineering. Can you explain that to me? Absolutely. So value engineering is

what we do when we are looking to reduce some costs on a project. So it's a term that we use where we look to maintain the value of the project, but also look for ways to reduce the cost. So, it's a good practice for us to do, and in this case, we work with a low bidder to reduce their cost a bit just by reviewing their bid in detail with them. Is that more just about the product that's used or the

negotiating service fees? What exactly of the value piece of this are you negotiating? Yeah, it could be all of those things. So, what we do is we'll ask our consultants to bring some ideas, we'll ask the contractor to bring some ideas, and they could be things such as changing a specification for a particular kind of tile or something like that. So there's various things. So we've executed some of those things with them that were relatively easy to do.

And we're going to continue to pursue some other value engineering ideas as we proceed with the project. Great. Thank you so much. Any other discussion? If not, we will go ahead and proceed to a vote, and this will go on the consent agenda for the school board. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Aye. Thank you very much, and that will go on the consent agenda.

Now we move on to item 4.02, Support Services Award of IFB 26-547 2027 Roof Renovation Program. May I have a motion to approve this item of 4.02? Yes, Madam Chair. I move that the Loudoun County School Board approve the contract award of IFB number 26-547 TOL, John W. Tolbert Elementary School Roofing Renovation Project to CHU Contracting, Inc. in the amount of

$1,686,384, and IFB 26-547 SEL, Seldens Landing Elementary School Roofing Renovation Project to Patuxent Roofing and Contracting, LLC in the amount of $1,641,850, and authorize the chair of the school board to sign the final contract documents upon presentation. Second. Thank you. This has been moved and seconded, and now it will be presented by Mr. Pascarelli, Director of Construction.

Thank you. So each year as part of lifecycle planning, new roofs are installed at various schools that we have based on the age of the roofs. These projects are funded through the approved cap budget, and will include John Tolbert and Seldens Landing Elementary School this coming summer. We have a competitive bid process here. We recommend approval to the low bidders identified in the item. Happy to answer any questions. Any discussion? Yes, Mr. Pepper. I find it interesting that you bid these as separate projects and not a single

project. Is there a reason for that? There is. So we found that we get better competition that way. So we do have several really good roofing contractors that work with us, so it gives us an opportunity to have the work distributed in such a way to the lowest bidder on each of them. So we found that we bid these sequentially, sometimes one day, then the next day we do the next one, and that way we think we get our best pricing and we get the best participation we can with our roofing vendors.

Thank you. Thank you very much, and I guess we will proceed to a vote to put on consent. All those in favor say aye. Aye. Aye. Thank you. We move on to our information items. We will now move on to 5.01, Business and Financial Services, State Cost Per Pupil for Tuition Purposes. This item is presented by Casey Jones, Director of Budget and Financial Analytics. Thank you.

Good afternoon. Section 22.1-5 of Virginia Code authorizes public school divisions to charge tuition for non-resident students, and per school board policy 4010, tuition fees, LCPS uses a state calculation to determine these tuition costs. And with the Board of Supervisors taking a final action on the school's FY27 budget earlier this month, we are now able to finalize tuition rates for this school year. Based on the state calculation, this would be $19,086 for out-of-county students and

$26,655 for out-of-state students. Unless otherwise directed, this item will be brought back to the FNO Committee on December 8th as either an action or consent item. Thank you. Thank you. Any discussion? Ms. Ricardi. Thank you, Madam Chair. Could we see the five-year trend on this? I know that they've been going up incrementally, but I don't know by how much, so either as a question, I guess, just an email response, or if

you want to bring it back at the next meeting, whatever we want to do. I'm good with either. We can provide that, yes. All right, great. Thank you. I would also like to mention, there's no document here to look at. And per Ms. Ricardi's request, when it does come back, if you could have it as an attachment, that would be great. Is there any more discussion? No? Okay, so that was an information item,

and we look forward to seeing it at the next meeting. Thank you. We now move on to item 5.02, Business and Financial Services Renewal of RFP number R25100, Roof Repair Services. This item is being presented by Ms. Fillaw, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you. Good evening. I'm presenting to you this evening the second renewal option for this contract, which is for roof repair and maintenance

services on an as-needed basis. Earlier, you had an action item to replace entire roofs. In this instance, this is to repair those roofs as identified by our facilities operations team. Two vendors were awarded this contract, Autumn Contracting and Raintree Services, and they did not increase their rate to provide these services. This is being brought before you as the amount is expected to estimated value is

$500,000, with the contract effective from February 1, 2027, through January 31st, 2028. If approved, this will be brought forward as either an action item or consent item on your December 8th meeting with school board consent agenda on December 15th. Thank you. Any discussion? No? Okay. Is there anything-- I know these are repairs, but is there anything that you can upload in a document?

There is no document that would be uploaded here. Mm-hmm. The information is provided to you in the executive only with the proposals, the RFP, and the pricing information. Okay. Thank you. So this is an information item, so we look forward to seeing it at the next meeting. Thank you. Item number 5.03, Business and Financial Services Renewal of RFP number R24253, Benefits Consulting and Actuarial Services.

This item is being presented by Ms. Fillaw, Director of Procurement and Risk Management. Thank you. This was also a renewal. The current contract expires on February 28th, 2027. This is the third renewal option with AON to provide consulting services related to our benefits program, and this is paid for through the self-insurance funds with an estimated value of $346,000. That is no rate increase in their annual fee charged for those services.

If approved, this can be brought back as an action item or consent item on December 8th, 2026, and the school board consent agenda on December 15th, 2026. Thank you. Any discussion? Oh, Mr. Pepper. Thank you, Madam Chair. About how often do we use these actuarial services? The actuarial services themselves are used annually for some report preparation that is built into the $346,000.

Other fees that are charged is before putting out a solicitation for health insurance. They will do that for us. During the upcoming year, we do not expect to put out any benefits solicitation. Therefore, that is why the rate is $346,000. So is the amount of work that we are receiving for $346,000 greater than the amount of work that one person alone could do?

Yes, and also because while it's a single cost, it's a firm, so they have a team that is preparing our actuarial reports, and it's more than one report that we are receiving from them. As well as they are available to answer questions throughout the year based on their expertise that they have that we do not have in-house. Okay. That's fair. I just wanted to do, in my brain, a cost analysis of would we be better off doing with one person?

Because I think we can probably get a person for less than $346K, but if we're talking about specialists, I think that this is- And that's a good point because I was going to add that they do things other than the actuarial report. Based on the discussion, are you comfortable moving this to the Finance and Operations Committee meeting consent? I am. Yep. And if I may go back to 5.2 and ask that same question for the roof repair? Yes.

All right, great. Thank you so much. We'll move on to 5.04. Business and Financial Services Renewal of RFP R24254 American Sign Language Interpreter Services. This item is being presented by Ms. Fillaw, Director of Procurement Risk Management. Thank you. This is for American Sign Language services that are funded both through the

Director of Employee Benefits, the HRTD department, as well as special education. This is for services for interpreters if we have, for example, a hearing-impaired parent that needs American Sign Language interpretation to have a meeting. That's for these types of services. If a student is having an IEP session or something, that is what special ed will do is provide. We will bring in these outside consultants to provide American Sign Language interpretation. We do have multiple vendors listed on this.

The multiple vendors are listed to ensure that there's always an availability of someone to provide the services on an as-needed or as-scheduled basis. This is a renewal. This is the third renewal option for this contract. The new contract is effective March 1, 2027, through February 29th, 2028. And if approved, this can be brought forward as an action item or consent item on your December 8th meeting and on the school board consent agenda on December 15th, 2026.

Thank you. Any discussion? Oh, I thought we had a discussion about this previously. Was this brought to us in the previous meeting or the one before that? or one-on-one meetings. We did have that discussion at one point. Okay. All right. Thank you. Well, based on the discussion, if the committee is comfortable moving this item forward to the next finance and operation consent? Yes? Yes, ma'am. Okay, we'll go ahead and do that. Thank you. This is for the various HVAC filters that we use in our schools that are handled by our facility operations team for replacement. You will see this one does have an attachment, as it was an IFB awarded by line item, and the awarded vendor on this contract, this is the fourth renewal option for this contract, and the awarded vendor is identified on the attachment, and the

value of this contract is $750,000, which is included in the FY27 facilities operating appropriated budget. There was no change in unit pricing for these filters. And the new contract's effective March 1, 2027, and once again, if approved, this may be brought forward as an action item or consent item on December 8th, 2026, and on the school board consent agenda on December 15th, 2026.

Thank you. Any discussion? No. Based on the discussion, I believe if we're comfortable moving it to consent, we'll go ahead and do that. Yes. Yes? Thank you very much. Now we continue on to 5.07, support services fiber easement at Elaine Thompson Elementary School. This item is being presented by Mr. Pasquarella, director of construction. Thank you. This is a request for an easement at the front of the school,

which would be used to provide fiber optic internet service to service this area. Documents have been reviewed by division counsel's office as well as support services engineering team. We do not see any impacts to the use of our site, and we recommend approval. Any discussion? Yes, Ms. McCarty. All right. I have a bunch of questions for you. So, I believe that our Cola Mills Drive is in an active VDOT and county study

right now to expand it. So I guess my first question is, if this is going right along the road, who's going to be responsible for moving these lines if they put them in and then they want to expand the road? So, I'll have to double-check, but I believe that the road widening study doesn't include this particular area of the road. I think it's down more towards

the other area of the road, but I'll find out for you. Okay. But the short answer to your question would be, we would not be responsible for moving this if any other work did occur. That's the responsibility of the vendor who's putting the lines in. All we're doing is giving them approval to be able to utilize some of our property to run that easement there, but we're not responsible for relocating if needed. Okay.

And does Policy 6355 apply at all to this? So this is not an electrical line. This is a fiber optic data line. Okay. I guess the part I'm concerned with is it's using our property for public use and utilities. I generally don't have a problem with this, just so you know. Sure. I just want to make sure that we're not in conflict with

our intent for 6355, but I'm assuming you guys have already looked at that, so I'm good with that. I just want to raise the pseudo question about whether or not we're good with that. I know we do this with other properties too, so again, I'm not super concerned with this. I just want to make sure that we're not getting ourselves into a situation where we've now put in public utility-ish lines on our property, and if there were any conflicts with that policy.

Yeah, we did review that. We believe that the policy is specific to electrical transmission, and this would not be applicable to that. Okay. And then there was this $1 purchase piece of that. Is that typical as well? Sometimes we see that in these easements, where there's essentially no cost to them for acquiring this property. And is there any risk management issues while they're doing this construction since they'd be on our property, or do we give the easement

and they bear the burden? If somebody gets injured on the job site, but it's the easement that we have. They carry the insurance during the course of that work. Okay. All right. Thank you for that. I appreciate it. Any other discussion? No. I am familiar with that area, and I know there's a lot of construction going on right now, and they're one lane on each side, so it's very tight.

So I'm just curious, this really doesn't have anything to do with it. It's not going to interfere with the kids getting to school or anything, is it? No, absolutely not. No. When we approve these types of things, we make sure that we understand when we'll be doing work and make sure that they don't interfere with any traffic. They have to keep our bus loop entries open at all times, those kinds of things. So we manage through those parts and pieces. Thank you. Thank you for clarifying. Of course.

Is everybody okay with consent for this item? Yes. Yes? Okay. We'll go ahead and put that on the Finance and Operation Committee meeting as a consent item. Thank you. We are at new business. had looked at last time, and I don't know if you guys have any questions. I know I just sent it this afternoon, so you probably haven't had a chance to even look at it, and that's totally fine. I just wanted just to let you know that we did talk about that Policy 4310 sample document, and I had pulled the information from that and from the sole source contract list from the website and put it in there. So, happy to answer questions about that at another time or later on whenever we get to

it, but that was just an example of, I think, what I was looking for. I think it encompasses the data that would be most useful as we're looking through the smaller purchase items for that policy. So just want to put that on the record that we've submitted that. Thank you, Ms. Ricardi. Is there any other new business to discuss today? No. Well, then we move on to adjournment if there's no further business.
